newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Don looks to London for overseas expansion.
newsitem.headline: Don looks to London for overseas expansion.

text.p: South African hotels firm Don Group is close to clinching its first overseas deal by buying a block of flats in London's fashionable Hyde Park area.
The firm specialises in providing self-catering apartments for customers, who are mainly business travellers, on longer stays rather than one-bedroom full service hotels.

"There are still some things that could go wrong, but they are keen sellers (of the property) and we are keen buyers," Brendan Tiernan, Don managing director told Reuters at a launch of the firm's latest hotel in Johannesburg.
If all goes well the deal could be sealed within two weeks, he added.
Tiernan said the London site would initially be aimed at attracting business travellers from the group's existing corporate clients, such as De Beers and Anglo American.
In South Africa, Don has capitalised on a boom in demand for long-stay apartments. Earlier this year Don bought the Trafalgar chain from Trafalgar Courts (Pty) Ltd for 72 million rand.

The market is also buoyant elsewhere. U.S. market research firm Smith Travel Research has estimated demand in the U.S. has outstripped supply by two to one over the past five years. Both Marriott and Choice Hotels International will launch mid-market extended stay brands this year.
Tiernan said the firm's longer-term ambitions lay in setting up an Australian joint-venture and then a possible move into other European cities, such as Paris.
Don chairman Marc Wainer said the firm would consider a share issue to raise the cash for the start of its overseas expansion or could explore other options such as bank loans.
"We have got various financing options and we are now just looking at them," he told Reuters.
Don executives also met up with British entrepreneur Richard Branson when he recently visited South Africa to publicise his Virgin Atlantic Airways' new route from London to Johannesburg.
Tiernan said no concrete deals had been discussed, but that Don would like to seal a tie-up with the airline and its hotels. "(Branson) loved our product," he said.
